advice: If lower leaves turn yellow with brown rings, it is likely early blight: remove affected leaves and spray Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre of water every 10 days. If leaves are evenly pale yellow, it is likely nitrogen deficiency: apply urea or well-rotted compost. Avoid overwatering.

problem: Leaf curl virus spread by whitefly
advice: Pull out and destroy badly affected plants. Control whitefly with yellow sticky traps and neem oil 5 ml per litre. If whitefly is high, spray Imidacloprid 0.3 ml per litre. Use virus-resistant varieties next season.
Install pheromone traps (5 per acre) and pick and destroy bored fruits. Spray neem oil 5 ml per litre. For heavy fruit borer attack, spray Emamectin benzoate 0.4 g per litre.

problem: Fruit rot or blossom end rot
advice: Black patch at the bottom of the fruit usually means calcium shortage from uneven watering: water regularly and spray calcium nitrate 5 g per litre. For soft fungal rot, remove infected fruits and spray Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre.

Spray Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre at first sign of spots. In cool, cloudy, humid weather (late blight risk) spray Metalaxyl + Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre. Remove infected leaves and avoid irrigation in the evening.
Apply balanced NPK fertilizer and keep soil moist but not waterlogged. If yellow leaves have dark rings, spray Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre.
Spray Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre mixed with a sticker every 10 to 15 days. Avoid dense planting and excess nitrogen.
Check soil moisture and irrigate lightly but regularly. If the bulb base is rotting, remove those plants, improve drainage, and drench soil with Carbendazim 1 g per litre.
Thrips cause silvery streaks on leaves. Use blue sticky traps and spray Fipronil 1.5 ml per litre or neem oil 5 ml per litre.
Install pheromone traps (5 per acre) for pink bollworm and destroy damaged bolls. For aphids or jassids spray neem oil 5 ml per litre; for heavy attack spray Imidacloprid 0.3 ml per litre.
Spray 1 percent magnesium sulphate (10 g per litre) and 2 percent urea (20 g per litre). Avoid waterlogging.
If yellow powder appears in stripes on leaves, it is yellow rust: spray Propiconazole 1 ml per litre. If the whole field is pale, apply a top dose of urea after irrigation.
For eye-shaped spots (blast) spray Tricyclazole 0.6 g per litre. For brown spots, apply potash and spray Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre. Avoid excess nitrogen.
Install pheromone traps and remove dead hearts. Spray Chlorantraniliprole 0.3 ml per litre if damage is high.
Remove and destroy affected plant parts. Spray Chlorantraniliprole 0.3 ml per litre or neem oil 5 ml per litre at early stage.
Remove infected plants early. Control whitefly, which spreads the virus, with yellow sticky traps and Thiamethoxam 0.2 g per litre. Use resistant varieties next season.
Remove badly affected plants. Spray neem oil 5 ml per litre. For thrips spray Fipronil 1.5 ml per litre; for mites spray wettable sulphur 3 g per litre.
Remove infected fruits and twigs. Spray Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre or Copper oxychloride 3 g per litre every 10 to 15 days.

problem: Nutrient deficiency, overwatering or early disease
advice: Check that the soil is not waterlogged. Apply balanced fertilizer or compost. If spots or rings appear on yellow leaves, spray Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre.
Remove affected leaves and spray Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre or Copper oxychloride 3 g per litre. Avoid wetting leaves while irrigating.
Check soil moisture first. If the soil is wet and plants still wilt, it may be wilt disease: remove affected plants and drench soil with Carbendazim 1 g per litre. Improve drainage.
Use yellow sticky traps and spray neem oil 5 ml per litre as a first step. If the attack is heavy, ask your local agriculture officer for the right insecticide for your crop.
Remove badly affected plants. Use yellow sticky traps and spray neem oil 5 ml per litre to control whitefly and thrips.
Remove and destroy rotting parts. Improve drainage and spray Copper oxychloride 3 g per litre.
